hints: Notice the $110^{\circ}$ in the diagram is the angle between the two second-order beams, so the diffraction angle $\theta$ for one beam from the straight-through direction is half of this.
Recall the grating equation $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ with line spacing $d = 1.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ and order $n = 2$ for second-order maxima.
Calculate $\sin 55^{\circ}$, multiply by $d$, then divide by $2$ to isolate the wavelength $\lambda$ in metres.
walkthrough: The grating equation uses the angle between a diffracted maximum and the central normal direction. The diagram shows $110^{\circ}$ between the upper and lower second-order beams, so each makes $\theta = 110^{\circ}/2 = 55^{\circ}$ with the normal.
State the governing rule for normal incidence: $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $d = 1.0 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ is the slit spacing and $n = 2$ for the second order.
This wavelength is in the visible range and matches the listed value $4.1 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$. This is option A.

options.A: With $\theta = 55^{\circ}$ and $n = 2$, $\lambda = d \sin\theta / n$ gives about $4.1 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
options.B: This value results from using $\sin 110^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 55^{\circ}$ in $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$.
options.C: This value is twice the correct wavelength and results from using $n = 1$ instead of $n = 2$.
options.D: This value results from using both $n = 1$ and the full $110^{\circ}$ angle instead of $55^{\circ}$.
